subject.title: [Bug]: Dashboard/agent fake tool calls with dmxapi model; native claude route returns incomplete terminal response

question: Should OpenClaw keep fake tool-call-shaped assistant text as warning-only/provider incompatibility, promote or retry it under bounded rules, or fail closed for agent turns when a model is expected to use tools?
rationale: The source-visible behavior is intentionally compatibility-preserving today, and changing it affects agent safety, local-model behavior, and provider compatibility; the native Claude incomplete-response path also needs owner review before one automated repair can safely choose the policy.

options.title: Bounded enforcement after live proof
options.body: Confirm the dmxapi/native Claude repro and then add a narrow retry, promotion, or fail-closed path only for provider/tool states that maintainers explicitly want to enforce.

options.title: Keep warning-only compatibility
options.body: Leave simulated tool-looking text as assistant text, document unsupported provider behavior clearly, and close this after native Claude incomplete output is separately fixed or ruled external.

options.title: Split provider repair from fake-tool policy
options.body: Move the native Claude incomplete-response work into a provider-specific issue while leaving #45049 to own the fake-tool enforcement decision.

recommendation.title: Bounded enforcement after live proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the dmxapi/native Claude repro and then add a narrow retry, promotion, or fail-closed path only for provider/tool states that maintainers explicitly want to enforce.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans agent runtime, terminal fallback classification, and Claude/Anthropic-provider support, making them the best available owner for the cross-surface policy call.
